questions.prompt: You are an hour into a single task. Claude Code warns it is out of room, and you want to keep going on the same task. What do you run?
options: /clear — free the memory and rebuild it
/compact — summarize the conversation and keep working, with the session's state intact
/exit — end the session so the state saves
questions.explanation: Same work, still going: compact replaces the long conversation with a summary while the files read and edits made stay tracked. Option A is tempting because freeing memory sounds like the fix, but it drops the state you still need. Option C ends rather than continues. Option D does not address the budget at all.

questions.prompt: You finished one task and are starting an unrelated one. The session's memory is full. What is the right move?
options: /compact so the old work is summarized and kept
/clear so the new task starts with an empty memory
Keep going — unused history is harmless
questions.explanation: The new task does not use the old task's history, so clearing stops you paying for it every turn. Option A is tempting as the safe-sounding choice, but it keeps a summary the new task will never read. Option C ends and resumes the same full session. Option D is the misconception: history competes for room and is re-paid on every turn.

questions.prompt: You ended a session with `/exit` and closed the terminal. Next morning you want to continue exactly where you stopped. What do you run?
options: Start Claude Code fresh — sessions are not saved
`claude --continue` — resume the most recent session with its state
Re-paste your last message into a new session
questions.explanation: `/exit` saves the session to disk, and `--continue` brings it back with the summary, files, and edits. Option A is the tempting belief that closing the terminal loses everything. Option C starts a new session and rebuilds by hand. Option D is a command for a running session, not a launch flag.

questions.prompt: You type `/clear`, then ask Claude Code what it remembers. It remembers nothing, yet the session is still open. Which statement is correct?
options: The session ended when you cleared it
`/clear` wipes the session's memory; a session can be alive with an empty memory, and `/exit` is what ends and saves it
The tool can scroll back through the transcript, so nothing is really lost
questions.explanation: The session is the state; `/clear` empties that state but does not end the session, and `/exit` is the operation that ends and saves. Option A is the tempting merge of clearing with exiting. Option C overstates it — the tool was not deleted. Option D confuses the transcript on disk with what the tool can currently see.
